blocks.text: Rheumatological disorders, also known as rheumatic diseases, comprise a diverse group of conditions that primarily affect the joints, bones, muscles, tendons, ligaments, and connective tissues. Many are driven by autoimmune and inflammatory processes, often leading to multi-organ involvement.

blocks.text: These diseases are usually chronic, may cause long-term disability, and often require multidisciplinary care. Management involves immunosuppressive therapy, including corticosteroids, conventional DMARDs, and biological agents. Accurate diagnosis and thorough assessment are crucial for guiding safe and effective treatment.

blocks.text: Before initiating DMARDs or biologics, it is essential to conduct liver and renal function tests, a chest X-ray, and screen for tuberculosis, HIV, and hepatitis B and C to rule out latent infections and ensure the safety of treatment.
